subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term request — packaging options
messages:
From: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@arcadiahealth.com, karim.r@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-contract uplift + co-term request

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our usage is trending above the committed band and the team wants to accelerate the next tranche of capacity. Two asks from procurement and finance: 1) can we add a mid-contract uplift for an additional 20% capacity and 2) can we align the new uplift to our existing contract term (co-term) instead of having a separate 12mo start?

They are sensitive to headline price movement — procurement asked whether any transitional credit or phased billing is possible while we normalize usage. I attached a short Q1 usage extract.

We’re hoping to finalize this week. Can you share the packaging options and an indicative delta to ARR?

Best,
Emily
Emily Nguyen
Head of AI Platform, Arcadia Health
emily.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com

Attachments: usage_report_Q1_2027.csv (CSV, 24KB)

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, procurement@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-30T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term request

Emily —

Thanks for the detail and the usage export — helpful. Quick reply with three pragmatic paths (short summary below, pricing matrix attached):

1) Instant uplift (simple top-up): +20% reserved capacity applied immediately, price = current committed rate for first 3 months, then full uplift rate thereafter. Minimal ops work; pro-rated invoice for month of change.

2) Phased uplift with transitional credit: split the +20% into two tranches (10% now, 10% in 60 days). For the first 60 days we provide a temporary 25% transitional credit on the incremental units to smooth ARR impact. At the second tranche we normalize to full rate.

3) Co-term + annualize: annualize the uplift over the remainder of your contract so the delta to ARR is smaller (effectively amortized). This requires a short amendment so legal can sign off; we can apply a modest blended rate discount for the annualized portion.

Operational notes: we can implement 1 or 2 within 48 hours. Option 3 requires procurement and legal signoff and DocuSign (2–3 business days typical).

I attached an initial pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx with the exact numbers by tier and a draft SOW that captures the uplift SOW language. Ben and Olga, looping you in for discount cadence and legal redlines respectively.

Proposed next step: which path looks best for Arcadia? If procurement needs a template amendment I’ll start the DocuSign package.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0194

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB), Arcadia_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, procurement@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term request

Emily / Mina —

I ran the numbers off Mina’s matrix. Two practical notes from pricing:

- If Arcadia commits to the co-term and annualizes the uplift we can offer a blended 12% effective discount on the incremental units (reflects margin and operational smoothing).
- If you prefer the phased credit approach, we can increase the transitional credit to 30% for the first tranche but it would require a firm second-tranche activation within 60 days (we need that to protect utilization planning).

Mina — can you confirm whether Arcadia’s finance needs a custom invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) for the amortized path? I’ll draft a short amendment with the two price lines so legal has something to redline.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Expansion Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Quote snip from pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx: incremental-rate (after credits) = $0.028/token equivalent; amortized blended = $0.024/token equivalent (12% discount).

From: Karim Rasheed <karim.r@arcadiahealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-02T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift + co-term request

Mina / Ben —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement’s primary constraint: we cannot materially increase monthly cash outflow in Q2 given budget gating. Preference order: 1) amortized co-term (minimize ARR delta), 2) phased uplift with credit (but need precise cash flow figures), 3) instant uplift (last resort).

Two asks for your amendment:
- Show net monthly cash delta under each option (monthly invoice projection for next 6 months).
- Confirm whether the transitional credit can be applied as a bill credit (line item) rather than a retrospective rebate.

If you can send a short amendment + projected invoices we’ll circulate to legal/finance today.

Karim
Karim Rasheed
Director, Procurement — Arcadia Health
karim.r@arcadiahealth.com

Karim —

Appreciate the clarity on preferred path. Attached: 1) short amendment for co-term + annualization, 2) 6-month projected invoice runs for all three options (monthly line items), and 3) updated SOW with activation milestones. Key points:

- Amortized/co-term path: amortize incremental capacity over remaining 8 months of the contract, effective blended incremental rate = $0.024/token equivalent; estimated monthly cash delta = +$11,200 (month 1 through month 8). DocuSign link is included in the header of the amendment PDF if you want to route to legal.

- Phased uplift: first 60 days credit is applied as an invoice line-item credit (not retrospective rebate) per your ask; we show cash delta = +$6,500 (month 1) then +$12,800 (month 2) when tranche two ramps.

- Instant uplift: one-time prorated amount followed by normalized monthly +$17,400.

Next steps I propose: you indicate preference and we initiate DocuSign. If Arcadia accepts amortized co-term I’ll route the amendment to Karim + procurement for signature and ask legal (Olga) to prepare the short redline-safe clause.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if useful.

— Mina
